options.text: The printer connected elsewhere on the network is low on toner
options.explanation: Printer toner level has no relationship to a switch port's link state.

options.text: The building's HVAC plenum rating
options.explanation: Cable plenum rating is a fire-code requirement, not a cause of link flapping.

options.text: A CMOS battery failure on a nearby desktop
options.explanation: A desktop's CMOS battery has no effect on a switch port's link status.

questions.prompt: A laser printer produces a thin, repeating vertical defect line down every printed page at the same position. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: A repeating vertical line at a consistent position on every page is a classic symptom of a scratch, groove, or other defect on the imaging drum. Since the drum is usually part of the toner cartridge assembly, replacing that cartridge/imaging unit typically resolves it.

options.text: A scratched or damaged imaging drum, usually resolved by replacing the toner cartridge/imaging unit
options.explanation: Correct. A repeating defect at a fixed interval matches the circumference of a damaged drum.

options.text: A loose network cable
options.explanation: A network cable issue would affect the print job reaching the printer, not create a repeating physical print defect.

options.text: Low input voltage from the wall outlet
options.explanation: Voltage issues would more likely cause the printer to malfunction entirely, not produce a precise repeating line pattern.

options.text: An outdated wireless driver on the print server
options.explanation: A driver issue would not produce a physically repeating defect tied to the drum's rotation.

questions.prompt: An inkjet printer's output has become noticeably faded and streaky compared to normal. What should the technician try first?
questions.explanation: Faded, streaky inkjet output commonly results from clogged print head nozzles or a nearly empty ink cartridge. Running the printer's built-in head-cleaning cycle, and replacing the cartridge if needed, is the standard first response.

options.text: Run the printer's head-cleaning cycle and check/replace the ink cartridge
options.explanation: Correct. Clogged nozzles and low ink are the most common causes of faded, streaky inkjet output.

options.text: Replace the imaging drum
options.explanation: Imaging drums are a laser printer component; inkjet printers do not use them.

options.text: Update the DNS server's TXT record
options.explanation: DNS configuration has no effect on physical print quality.

options.text: Increase the network switch's PoE budget
options.explanation: PoE power budget on a switch is unrelated to inkjet print head or ink cartridge condition.

questions.prompt: Which TWO symptoms are strong indicators of a failing power supply unit (PSU)?
questions.explanation: Random shutdowns under load and a burning smell from the case are both classic warning signs of a failing power supply. Faded printer output and dead monitor pixels are unrelated symptoms tied to a printer and a display panel, not the PSU.

options.text: Random shutdowns under load
options.explanation: Correct. Unexpected shutdowns under load are a common PSU failure symptom.

options.text: A burning smell coming from the case
options.explanation: Correct. A burning smell can indicate a failing PSU or other electrical component.

options.text: Faded output on printed pages
options.explanation: Faded print output points to a printer consumable/head issue, not the PC's power supply.

options.text: Dead pixels on an external monitor
options.explanation: Dead pixels are a display panel defect, unrelated to the power supply.

questions.prompt: Which TWO symptoms are most consistent with a hard drive that is beginning to fail?
questions.explanation: Grinding or clicking noises during operation and a S.M.A.R.T. failure warning at boot are both classic indicators of an ailing hard drive. Screen burn-in and switch port flapping are unrelated symptoms tied to a display panel and network hardware, respectively.

options.text: Grinding or clicking noises during operation
options.explanation: Correct. Unusual mechanical noise often indicates a failing hard drive.

options.text: A S.M.A.R.T. failure warning at boot
options.explanation: Correct. S.M.A.R.T. warnings are a predictive indicator of drive failure.

options.text: Burn-in on the display
options.explanation: Burn-in is a display panel issue, unrelated to hard drive health.

options.text: A switch port flapping up and down
options.explanation: Port flapping is a network hardware/cabling symptom, unrelated to a hard drive's condition.

questions.prompt: Which TWO factors commonly cause poor or intermittent wireless connectivity on a mobile device?
questions.explanation: A physically damaged antenna or charging/data port that also carries antenna traces can degrade signal reception, and interference from other nearby wireless devices operating on overlapping channels can disrupt connectivity. A printer's toner level and an unrelated RAID rebuild on a server have no effect on a mobile device's wireless connection.

options.text: A physically damaged antenna or port
options.explanation: Correct. Physical antenna damage directly degrades wireless reception.

options.text: Interference from other nearby wireless devices
options.explanation: Correct. Overlapping channels and RF interference commonly disrupt wireless connectivity.

options.text: A low toner level in an office printer
options.explanation: Printer toner level has no relationship to a mobile device's wireless connectivity.

options.text: A RAID array rebuilding on an unrelated file server
options.explanation: A server-side RAID rebuild does not directly cause a mobile device's wireless connectivity problems.

questions.prompt: A network printer is producing garbled, nonsensical characters instead of the intended document text. Which TWO causes should be investigated first?
questions.explanation: Garbled print output most often traces back to an outdated or incorrect print driver that is miscommunicating the page description language with the printer, or to a corrupt/incompatible spool file for that job. A loose network cable would more likely prevent the job from printing at all, and low toner produces faded output, not garbled text.

options.text: An outdated or incorrect print driver installed for the printer
options.explanation: Correct. A mismatched driver is a leading cause of garbled print output.

options.text: A damaged or corrupt spool file for the print job
options.explanation: Correct. Spooler corruption can cause a job to print as garbled data.

options.text: A loose network cable causing the print job to queue
options.explanation: A loose cable would more likely prevent the job from printing at all rather than cause garbled characters.

options.text: A low remaining toner level
options.explanation: Low toner typically causes faded or light print, not garbled text.

questions.prompt: True or false: A desktop that shows a completely blank screen with no POST beep and no fan spin immediately after pressing the power button is most likely suffering from a corrupted print spooler.
questions.explanation: This is false. A completely blank screen with no beep and no fan activity at power-on points to a power delivery problem (such as a failed PSU, a loose power connector, or a dead motherboard), not a software-level issue like the print spooler, which would only matter after the OS has fully booted.

questions.prompt: A user reports that internal file shares on the local network work fine, but no websites will load, even though the computer has a valid IP address, subnet mask, and gateway. What should be checked first?
questions.explanation: When local (LAN) resources work but internet resources fail despite valid IP configuration, DNS resolution failure or a problem with the router/gateway's WAN connection to the ISP are the most likely causes, since local traffic does not depend on either of those.

options.text: Whether DNS resolution is working and whether the gateway has a working WAN connection to the ISP
options.explanation: Correct. Local resources bypass DNS/WAN dependency, so a failure isolated to internet access points to DNS or the WAN uplink.

options.text: Whether the printer's maintenance kit needs replacement
options.explanation: Printer maintenance is unrelated to a computer's internet access.

options.text: Whether the CPU is properly seated in its socket
options.explanation: A seating issue would typically prevent the system from booting at all, not selectively block internet access while LAN access works.

options.text: Whether the RAID array needs to be rebuilt
options.explanation: A RAID array issue on unrelated storage would not selectively block internet access while leaving local file shares reachable.

questions.prompt: A technician is following the standard troubleshooting methodology while resolving a user's reported issue. Arrange the phases of this methodology in the correct order, from first contact with the problem to final closure.
questions.explanation: The generally accepted troubleshooting methodology starts with identifying the problem by gathering information, then forming and testing a theory of probable cause, then establishing and implementing a plan of action, then verifying full functionality, and finally documenting the findings and outcome for future reference.

items.text: Identify the problem by gathering information from the user and the system
Establish a theory of probable cause, questioning the obvious first
Test the theory to determine the actual cause
Establish a plan of action and implement the solution
Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures if applicable
Document findings, actions taken, and outcomes
